172.01 CREATION AND MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created the North Olmsted Tax Incentive Review Council
(hereinafter referred to as the “TIRC”), comprised of the following members:
   (a)   The Mayor, or his/her designee;
   (b)   A member of Council appointed by the President of Council;
   (c)   The Cuyahoga County Auditor or his/her designee;
   (d)   The Director of Finance, or his/her designee;
   (e)   One individual appointed jointly by the North Olmsted Board of
Education and the Polaris Joint Vocational School District; and
   (f)   Two members of the public appointed by the Mayor with the concurrence
of the City Council.
   At least four members of the TIRC shall be residents of the City of North
Olmsted, and at least one of the two public members appointed by the Mayor
shall be a minority. As used in this section, a "minority" is an individual who
is African-American, Hispanic, or Native American. Notwithstanding the
foregoing provisions, if a member of the North Olmsted Housing Council is
appointed to membership on the TIRC, then his or her term on the TIRC shall
expire on the same date that his/her term on the North Olmsted Housing Council
expires. The City Council member may serve for a term of four years, or as may
be appointed by the President of the City Council, and so long as said
appointee is and remains a member of City Council.
(Ord. 2013-68. Passed 9-3-13.)
172.02 DUTIES.
   (a)   The County Auditor or the County Auditor’s designee shall serve as the
chairperson of the TIRC. The TIRC shall meet at the call of the chairperson. At
the first meeting of Council, Council shall select a vice-chairperson.
Attendance by a majority of the members of the TIRC constitutes a quorum to
conduct business.
   (b)   Annually, the TIRC shall review all agreements granting exemptions
from property taxation under Ohio R.C. Chapter 725 or 1728 or under Ohio R.C.
3735.671, 5709.62, 5709.63, or 5709.632, or under Chapter
171 of the North Olmsted Codified Ordinances, and any performance or audit
reports required to be submitted pursuant to those agreements. With respect to
each agreement, as referenced in Section  171.06  of the North Olmsted Codified
Ordinances and pursuant to state law, the TIRC shall determine whether the
owner of the exempted property has complied with the agreement, taking into
consideration any fluctuations in the business cycle unique to the owner’s
business, and, on the basis of such determinations, submit to City Council
written recommendations for continuation, modification, or cancellation of the
agreement.
   Upon the request of the TIRC, the County Auditor, the Housing Officer
appointed pursuant to Section
171.04 of the North Olmsted Codified Ordinances, the owner of a new or
remodeled structure or improvement, and City Council shall supply the TIRC with
any information reasonably necessary for the TIRC to make the determinations
required under this paragraph, including returns filed pursuant to Ohio R.C.
5711.02.
   (c)   Annually, the TIRC shall review the compliance of each recipient of a
tax exemption under Ohio R.C. Chapter 725 or 1728 or Ohio R.C. 3735.67,
5709.40, 5709.41, 5709.62, 5709.63, 5709.632, 5709.73, or 5709.78 with the
nondiscriminatory hiring policies developed by the City Council pursuant to
Ohio R.C. 5709.832.
(Ord. 2007-8. Passed 2-20-07.)
172.03  MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS.
   No individual shall be disqualified from membership on the TIRC by reason of
his membership, past or present, on the North Olmsted Housing Council.
(Ord. 99-34. Passed 5-18-99.)
CHAPTER 173
Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program
173.01   Established.
173.02   Interest subsidies provided.
173.03   Subsidies payable from interest on City funds.
173.04   Interest subsidies subject to annual appropriations.
173.05   Discrimination prohibited.
173.06   Housing Council's duties.
173.07   Agreements with lending institutions.
 
CROSS REFERENCES
Housing assistance - see Ohio Const., Art. VIII, Sec. 16
 
 
173.01 ESTABLISHED.
   Council hereby establishes, pursuant to Article VIII, Section 16 of the Ohio
Constitution, a "Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program". The Home
Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program shall be administered by the Director
of Finance and the Housing Officer of the City, in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter and eligibility criteria and procedural rules and
regulations to be recommended by the North Olmsted Housing Council for approval
by this Council, which regulations shall not be inconsistent or in conflict
with any provision of this chapter.
(Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.02 INTEREST SUBSIDIES PROVIDED.
   Under the Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program, the City intends
to provide an interest subsidy for certain loans to resident owners of record
of properties in the City made by lending institutions that have entered into
an agreement with the City in accordance with Section
173.04, to the extent that moneys not raised by taxation are appropriated for
that purpose in accordance with Section
173.04 and on the following terms and conditions:
   (a)   Each loan shall be for the purpose of rehabilitating, remodeling or
otherwise improving a single-family or two-family residence or a residential
condominium unit located within the City and shall be made by a lending
institution that has entered into an agreement with the City in accordance with
Section
173.04 to the resident owner or owners of record of such residential real
property. The improvements to be made shall be real property improvements.
   (b)   The interest subsidy provided shall be equal to or less than three
percent (3%), as determined in accordance with the eligibility criteria
described in Section
173.03.
   (c)   The interest subsidy shall be provided for a period equal to the
lesser of:
      (1)   The term of the loan or
      (2)   Twenty-four months.
   (d)   The interest subsidy may be granted for all or a portion of the
principal amount of a loan; provided that the principal amount with respect to
which interest subsidies are granted to each resident owner shall not exceed:
      (1)   Fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) for that owner during each
calendar year and
      (2)   Two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000) for that owner during
the life of this Program.
   (e)   Interest subsidies shall be provided on a first-come, first-served
basis to residents who meet the eligibility criteria to be established as
described in Section
173.03, to the extent that moneys not raised by taxation are appropriated by
Council for such purpose in accordance with Section
173.04.
      (Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.03 SUBSIDIES PAYABLE FROM INTEREST ON CITY FUNDS.
   Interest subsidies granted under this Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy
Program shall be payable from interest earnings on investments in the General
Fund or other funds designated by Council and invested specifically to fund the
Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program. No interest subsidy shall be
paid from moneys raised by taxation and the City's general obligation and full
faith and credit shall not be pledged to the payment of any interest subsidy,
unless the City has first complied with the requirements set forth in Ohio R.C.
176.04 for the City to issue general obligations or expend moneys raised by
taxation to provide, or assist in providing, housing pursuant to Article VIII,
Section 16 of the Ohio Constitution.
(Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.04 INTEREST SUBSIDIES SUBJECT TO ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS.
   The City's obligation to pay interest subsidies under this Home Improvement
Loan Interest Subsidy Program is subject to annual appropriations. After the
first year during which the City has paid interest subsidies, the City shall
not appropriate moneys for new interest subsidies during each year until it has
first appropriated moneys to continue the interest subsidies approved during
the immediately preceding year through the remainder of the reduced rate period
applicable to those interest subsidies.
(Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.05 DISCRIMINATION PROHIBITED.
   The Home Improvement Loan Subsidy Program shall be administered in such a
manner so that the City does not encourage, contribute to or participate in an
unlawful discriminatory practice under Ohio R.C. 4112.02(H), as amended from
time to time, or discriminate against families with children.
(Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.06 HOUSING COUNCIL'S DUTIES.
   The North Olmsted Housing Council is hereby authorized and directed:
   (a)   To make annual recommendations to Council concerning the eligibility
criteria for interest subsidies, which criteria shall be established by Council
by separate ordinance;
   (b)   To recommend procedural rules and regulations for approval by Council;
   (c)   To create application forms and review applications; and
   (d)   Take all other related actions necessary to implement the Home
Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program which are consistent with this
chapter and the eligibility criteria and procedural rules and regulations to be
approved by Council.
      (Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
173.07 AGREEMENTS WITH LENDING INSTITUTIONS.
   The Mayor and the Director of Finance are hereby authorized to enter into an
agreement or agreements with any lending institution which has an office or
branch office in the City, for the purpose of implementing this Home
Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program. Each such agreement shall be signed
by the Mayor and the Director of Finance and approved by the Director of Law
and shall contain, at a minimum, provisions to the following effect which shall
be binding upon the lending institution and the City:
   (a)   The lending institution shall make such loans for the purpose of
rehabilitating, remodeling or otherwise improving single-family or two-family
residences, or residential condominium units within the City and shall make
such loans to the resident owner or owners of record of such residential
property.
   (b)   The lending institution shall agree to lend to each eligible owner of
record who meets its lending criteria at a reduced interest rate for the
principal amount with respect to which the City has approved an interest
subsidy, which interest rate:
      (1)   For the period with respect to which the City provides the interest
subsidy (the "reduced rate period") shall be below the then existing borrowing
rate applicable to that owner by an amount equal to the subsidy approved by the
City; and
      (2)   For the remaining term of the loan, if any, shall be equal to such
borrowing rate and shall not be increased due to the reduced rate during the
reduced rate period.
   (c)   The City shall agree to pay the lending institution during the reduced
rate period, an amount equal to the difference between:
      (1)   Interest on the principal amount of the loan with respect to which
the City has approved an interest subsidy at the borrowing rate applicable to
that borrower at the time of loan approval as certified by the lending
institution to the City; and
      (2)   Interest on the principal amount with respect to which the City has
approved an interest subsidy at the reduced rate to be paid by the owner of
record during the reduced rate period.
   (d)   The lending institution shall not be entitled to any interest subsidy
under this Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program unless, prior to the
closing of the loan, the owner of record has first received approval of his
application for participation in the Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy
Program from the Director of Finance and Housing Officer of the City.
   (e)   The lending institution shall not sell, assign or otherwise transfer
any loan made to an owner of record who is a participant in the Home
Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program during the reduced rate period
applicable to that loan.
   (f)   In making loans for which an interest subsidy will be provided under
this Program, the lending institution shall not discriminate against families
with children or encourage, contribute to or participate in any unlawful
discriminatory practice under Ohio R.C. 4112.02(H), as amended from time to
time. A copy of Ohio R.C. 4112.02(H), as it exists at the time the agreement is
entered into, may be attached to the agreement.
   (g)   The City shall not be liable to any lending institution in any manner
for the payment of the principal or interest (other than the interest subsidy
described above) on any loan for which an interest subsidy has been approved by
the City under the Home Improvement Loan Interest Subsidy Program, and any
delay in payment or default on the part of any borrower shall not in any manner
affect the agreement between the lending institution and the City.
   (h)   The City's obligations under this agreement:
      (1)   Shall be paid only from moneys which do not constitute moneys
raised by taxation; and
      (2)   Are not and do not constitute a general obligation of the City or a
pledge of the full faith and credit of the City; provided that such provision
need not be included in the agreement if the City has complied with the
requirements set forth in Ohio R.C. 176.04 for the City to issue general
obligations or expend moneys raised by taxation to provide, or assist in
providing, housing pursuant to Article VIII, Section 16 of the Ohio
Constitution.
         (Ord. 92-52. Passed 5-19-92.)
CHAPTER 174
Job Creation Grant Program
174.01   Purpose.
174.02   Definitions.
174.03   Eligibility.
174.04   Application procedures.
174.05   Economic Development Committee.
174.06   Grant requirements.
174.07   Grant terms.
 
 
174.01 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of the City of North Olmsted’s Job Creation Grant Program is to
provide an economic incentive for businesses to locate or expand within the
City. The Program specifically seeks to create and retain jobs pursuant to the
terms and conditions set forth in this Chapter. The Job Creation Grant Program
(“Program”) is an annual payment from the City’s non-tax generated revenues
(such as interest income, permit fees, service charges, and activity fees) to a
participating business based on a percentage of specified New Annual Payroll
arising from the creation of jobs located within North Olmsted.
(Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.02 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   “Business” means any nonprofit corporation as well as any enterprise,
activity, profession or undertaking of any nature conducted for profit or
ordinarily conducted for profit, whether by an individual, partnership,
association, limited liability company, corporation or any other entity.
   (b)   “New Annual Payroll” means the dollar amount of new or additional
payroll attributable to New Jobs.
      (Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.03 ELIGIBILITY.
   The following businesses are eligible to complete an application for the
Program:
   (a)   A business constructing, buying or leasing property within the City of
North Olmsted that has not had employees located in the City of North Olmsted
within the preceding one (1) year and that will create a New Annual Payroll in
excess of five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000).
   (b)    An existing business already located in the City of North Olmsted
that is expanding and that will create a New Annual Payroll in excess of five
hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) while maintaining its pre-application work-
force and annual payroll.
      (Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.04 APPLICATION PROCEDURES.
   Application forms for the Program are available from the Director of
Planning. Once a completed application and an application fee is received by
the Director of Planning, the Economic Development Committee will review the
application and make a recommendation regarding eligibility and appropriate
terms for the Grant to the Mayor. All grants must be approved by City Council.
After approval by Council, a Grant Agreement will be prepared by the City for
execution by the eligible business. The Grant Agreement must be executed before
the Business is eligible for any payment under the Program.
(Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.05 ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE.
   The Economic Development Committee shall be comprised of the Planning
Director, the Finance Director and one member of City Council appointed by the
Council President.
(Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.06 GRANT REQUIREMENTS.
   To be eligible to receive the Grant, businesses must:
   (a)   Commit to creating and maintaining a specified amount of New Annual
Payroll.
   (b)    Comply with the laws and ordinances of the City.
   (c)   Not be delinquent on any tax payment to the State of Ohio or any
political subdivision within the State of Ohio.
   (d)   Enter into a Grant Agreement with the City.
   (e)   Agree to solicit employment applications from qualified City residents
and consider those applications for employment positions that are available
during the term of the Grant Agreement.
   (f)    Comply with the terms of the Grant Agreement.
      (Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
174.07 GRANT TERMS.
   All Grant Agreements shall contain the following terms:
   (a)   An agreement to maintain a specific New Annual Payroll for a stated
number of years, not to exceed ten years.
   (b)    A stated amount of grant payment to be made or a formula to determine
the grant payment based upon New Annual Payroll.
   (c)    Acknowledgement that payments are payable only after the New Annual
Payroll has been maintained for one calendar year.
   (d)    A schedule for grant payments during the term of the Agreement if New
Annual Payroll is maintained.
   (e)   A requirement for the business to make an annual report on or before a
specified date each year during the term of the Agreement stating the New
Annual Payroll and all payroll generated within the City during the prior
calendar year. A filing fee for the annual report is required.
   (f)   Provisions governing the termination of the Grant Agreement including
a term that requires the business to return to the City all grant payments
received, if the business relocates outside of the City during the term of the
Grant Agreement.
      (Ord. 2007-102. Passed 9-4-07.)
CHAPTER 175
Division of Electronic Data Processing
   EDITOR’S NOTE: Former Chapter
175 was repealed by Ordinance 2004-04, passed February 17, 2004.
 
 
 
CHAPTER 176
Job Retention Grant Program
 
176.01   Purpose.
176.02   Definitions.
176.03   Eligibility.
176.04   Application procedures.
176.05   Economic Development Committee.
176.06   Grant requirements.
176.07   Grant terms.
 
176.01 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of the City of North Olmsted's Job Retention Grant Program is to
provide an economic incentive for businesses to remain or expand within the
City. The Program specifically seeks to retain and create jobs pursuant to the
terms and conditions set forth in this Chapter. The Job Retention Grant Program
("Program") is an annual payment from the City's non-tax generated revenues
(such as interest income, permit fees, service charges, and activity fees) to a
participating business based on a percentage of specified retained and/or new
annual payroll arising from the retention and/or creation of jobs located
within North Olmsted.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.02 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   "Business" means any nonprofit corporation as well as any enterprise,
activity, profession or undertaking of any nature conducted for profit or
ordinarily conducted for profit, whether by an individual, partnership,
association, limited liability company, corporation or any other entity.
 
   (b)   "Retained Annual Payroll" means the dollar amount of retained or
preserved payroll attributable to Retained Jobs.
 
   (c)   "New Annual Payroll" means the dollar amount of new or additional
payroll attributable to New Jobs.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.03 ELIGIBILITY.
   The following businesses are eligible to complete an application for the
Program:
   (a)   An existing business already located in the City of North Olmsted that
will maintain an Retained Annual Payroll in excess of $8,000,000.00.
   (b)   Retail Businesses are not eligible to complete an application and
participate in the Program unless requested to do so by the Director of
Planning and Development.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.04 APPLICATION PROCEDURES.
   Application forms for the Program are available from the Director of
Planning and Development. Once a completed application and an application fee
are received by the Director of Planning and Development, the Economic
Development Committee will review the application and make a recommendation
regarding eligibility and appropriate terms for the Grant to the Mayor. All
Grants must be approved by City Council. After approval by Council, a Grant
Agreement will be prepared by the City for execution by the eligible business.
The Grant Agreement must be executed before the Business is eligible for any
payment under the Program.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.05 ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE.
   The Economic Development Committee shall be comprised of the Planning and
Development Director, the Finance Director and one member of City Council
appointed by the Council President.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.06 GRANT REQUIREMENTS.
   To be eligible to receive the Grant, Businesses must:
   (a)    Commit to maintaining a specified amount of Retained Annual Payroll.
   (b)    Comply with the laws and ordinances of the City of North Olmsted.
   (c)   Not be delinquent on any tax payment to the State of Ohio or any
political subdivision within the State of Ohio.
   (d)   Enter into a Grant Agreement with the City of North Olmsted.
   (e)   Agree to solicit employment applications from qualified City of North
Olmsted residents and consider those applications for employment positions that
are available during the term of the Grant Agreement.
   (f)    Comply with the terms of the Grant Agreement.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
176.07 GRANT TERMS.
   All Grant Agreements shall contain the following terms:
   (a)   An agreement to maintain a specific Retained Annual Payroll for a
stated number of years, not to exceed ten (10) years.
   (b)    A stated amount of grant payment to be made or a formula to determine
the grant payment based upon Retained Annual Payroll.
   (c)    Acknowledgment that payments are payable only after the Retained
Annual Payroll has been maintained for one calendar year.
   (d)    A schedule for grant payments during the term of the Agreement if
Retained Annual Payroll is maintained.
   (e)   A requirement for the Business to make an Annual Report on or before a
specified date each year during the term of the Agreement stating the Retained
Annual Payroll and all payroll generated within the City during the prior
calendar year. A filing fee for the Annual Report is required.
   (f)   Provisions governing the termination of the Grant Agreement including
a term that requires the Business to return to the City of North Olmsted all
grant payments received, if the Business relocates outside of the City of North
Olmsted during the term of the Grant Agreement.
(Ord. 2016-76. Passed 8-16-16.)
 
CHAPTER 177
Community Access
177.01   Definitions.
177.02   Purpose.
177.03   Applications; review by Mayor’s designee.
177.04   Content regulations for signs and banners.
177.05   Content regulations for City Website.
177.06   Additional regulations for banners.
177.07   Priority in cases of conflict; time limits.
177.08   Appeals from decisions of Mayor’s designee.
177.09   Non-endorsement policy of City.
177.10   Content regulations for designated display cases and lawn areas.
177.11   Adoption of policy and procedure for City media and City website;
publication of regulations.
 
 
 
177.01 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   "City media", unless otherwise specified, means any of the following:
      (1)   The airspace located approximately 20-25 feet above Lorain Road
approximately mid-way between East Park and West Park Drives, and in the
vicinity of a certain CEI wire, or wires, which traverse that airspace above
Lorain Road from north to south;
      (2)   The changeable copy sign on Lorain Road adjacent to the Police
Station;
      (3)   The changeable copy sign at North Olmsted Park;
      (4)   Designated, nonpublic display cases located in the lobby area of
public buildings, including but not limited to City Hall;
      (5)   Designated and limited lawn areas located on public property, not
greater than thirty (30) feet in length, parallel to and not closer than ten
(10) feet of the public right of way, including but not limited to North
Olmsted park.
   (b)   "City website", means all announcement lists or boards on the City's
internet site, http://www.north-olmsted.com.
   (c)   "Community event" means any meeting, program, exhibition, assembly,
celebration, or other gathering which is either open to the general public or
to which at least thirty (30) residents of the City of North Olmsted have been
invited or are otherwise permitted to attend.
   (d)   "Community organization" means:
      (1)   Any non-profit corporation, which is tax exempt pursuant to IRC
Section 501(c)(3), or any not for profit unincorporated association, which:
         A.   Either has had a continuous presence in the City of North Olmsted
for at least the two-year period immediately preceding its application under
the provisions of this chapter, or whose membership is composed of at least
thirty (30) persons, with at least seventy-five percent (75%) of those persons
being residents of the City; and
         B.   Organizes, sponsors or otherwise supports community events; or
      (2)   Any agency of the United States of America, the State of Ohio, or
any political subdivision of the State of Ohio.
   (e)   "Presence in the City of North Olmsted" means that the organization
has an office in a building which is located in a commercial district of the
City.
   (f)   "Link" means a segment of text or a graphical item that serves as a
cross-reference between parts of a hypertext document or between files or
hypertext documents. (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.02 PURPOSE.
   (a)   The regulations in this chapter pertaining to the city media as
described in Section
177.01(a) are enacted to create nonpublic forums solely to further the
following limited purposes:
      (1)   To accommodate access by community organizations to these nonpublic
forums only for the purpose of announcing community events;
      (2)   To ensure that the announcements placed in or at these nonpublic
forums are of genuine community interest; and to ensure that these nonpublic
forums are easily accessible by community organizations;
       (3)   To designate limited locations on public property to provide for
community organizations to announce community events within parameters of
reasonable time, place and method restrictions to preserve esthetically
pleasing appearance of public property and to prevent visual clutter;
       (4)   To restrict access to nonpublic display cases in order to provide
priority to official public notification, agenda, announcements, and general
information; to provide community organizations space, if available, to display
literature announcing community events.
 
   (b)   The regulations in this chapter pertaining to the City's website as
described in Section
177.01(b) are enacted to create a nonpublic forum solely to further the
following limited purposes:
      (1)   To allow links from the City's internet site, http://www.north-
olmsted.com, internet sites of community organizations where links to such
sites positively promote the welfare and development of North Olmsted. Such
organizations may include, but not be limited to, organizations that meet the
City's goal of:
         A.   Promoting tourism;
         B.   Enhancing neighborhood development;
         C.   Enhancing youth development;
         D.   Promoting a positive image of the overall quality of life in
North Olmsted.
            (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.03 APPLICATIONS; REVIEW BY MAYOR’S DESIGNEE.
   (a)   Community organizations desiring to announce community events through
the City media or wishing to link to the City's website, shall make an
application to the City in writing, on a form prepared by the City. The Mayor
or his designee shall be the City official responsible for:
      (1)   Receiving and acting upon applications for access to the nonpublic
forums;
      (2)   With respect to the banners and changeable copy signs, determining
the maximum number of space, in characters, available for messages; and
      (3)   Authorizing written opinions whenever an application is denied;
explaining the grounds for denial.
   The Mayor shall designate a member of his staff to review and act upon
applications made pursuant to this chapter.
   (b)   Applications must be completed and signed no later than thirty (30)
days prior to the time the applicant requests that the announcement be made.
   (c)   Applications shall contain all information requested by the form
adopted by the City, including but not limited to the name and address of the
community organization representative responsible for submitting the
application and supplying any additional information necessary to the
processing of the application. Additionally, the applications for signs and
banners shall include the date the announcement is requested.
   (d)   Applications must conform to the regulations of this chapter in all
particularities. If the Mayor's designee, upon review of the application,
discovers any irregularity or defect therein, the application shall be denied
for failure to conform to these regulations.
   (e)   Applications shall be acted upon by the Mayor's designee, in writing,
within ten working days following the date of filing of the application.
Applications shall be routinely granted, and may not be denied by the Mayor's
designee, unless the application, or the proposed announcement, fails to
conform to at least one express provisions of this chapter. Decisions denying
an application shall be mailed to the applicant by certified mail, return
receipt requested. No application shall be denied unless the reason for denial
has first been reviewed by the Director of Law. (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-
10.)
177.04 CONTENT REGULATIONS FOR SIGNS AND BANNERS.
   The City is establishing a nonpublic forum in the airspace above the City
right-of-way at the location described in Section
177.01(a)(1), and with regard to the two changeable copy signs as described in
Section
177.01(a)(2) and (3). Only the announcement of community events by community
organizations is permitted in such nonpublic forums. Accordingly, any proposed
message must be a single event announcement. The City will publish only the
date, time, and location of such an event open to the public, along with the
title of the event, so long as the title fits within the number and size of
characters available on a banner as defined below in Section
177.06. Applications containing titles that are too lengthy will be denied. No
title will be edited by City personnel. Exclusionary criteria for evaluating
community announcements may include, but not be limited to, the following:
   (a)   No announcements communicating events sponsored by a business-for-
profit.
   (b)   No announcements communicating imminent lawless action, false
statements of fact, fighting words, profanity, or obscenity.
   (c)    No announcements communicating discriminatory or disparaging persons
on the basis of race, gender, national origin, age, religion, economic status,
handicapped status, or sexual orientation.
      (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.05 CONTENT REGULATIONS FOR CITY WEBSITE.
   (a)   The City is establishing a nonpublic forum with regard to the City's
website as described in Section
177.01(b). Exclusionary criteria for evaluating internet sites may include, but
not be limited to, the following:
      (1)   No links to any organization whose primary purpose is business-for-
profit.
      (2)   No organizations promoting tourism outside the City of North
Olmsted. (Exceptions may be made for State-wide tourist organizations whose
internet sites include North Olmsted among other content)
      (3)   No links to sites that offend community standards of decency. Links
will not be granted to internet sites containing textual or graphical content
that appeals primarily to prurient sexual interests or is obscene, or
pornographic.
      (4)    No links to sites communicating imminent lawless action, false
statements of fact, fighting words, profanity, or obscenity.
      (5)   No links to sites communicating discriminatory or disparaging
persons in the basis of race, gender, national origin, age, religion, economic
status, handicapped status or sexual orientation.
   (b)   No Public Forum or Market for Advertising. The City's internet site
does not comprise either a public forum for the advocacy, exchange and
discussion of opinions, or a free venue for businesses-for-profit to advertise
for commercial gain, nor is the City obligated to provide such a forum by
virtue of its presence on the internet. In fact, the City may elect at any
time, now or in the future, to remove all links to any internet sites and deny
all requests for links for an indefinite period.
   (c)   Removal of Links. The City may, in its sole discretion, remove any
link to its internet site at any time, with no notice to the sponsoring
organization. Links may be removed for reasons including, but not limited to,
the following:
      (1)   Failure to effectively and positively promote the City's image. The
City may remove a link if, in its sole judgment, either the sponsoring
organization or its internet site do not effectively and positively promote the
City's image or support the goals stated in Section
177.02(b) of this policy;
      (2)   Evidence of criminal activity.  The City may remove a link if
information comes to its attention that in the City's sole judgment,
compromises evidence of criminal activity, whether or not such activity can be
inferred from the organization's website itself;
      (3)   Publication of injurious, defamatory, or abusive communication
attributed to an organization. The City may remove a link if communication
comes to its attention that is attributable to the organization or its officers
or representatives that in the City's sole judgment, compromises statements
that are slanderous, defamatory, abusive or otherwise harmful to individuals or
groups, particularly with regard to race, national origin, age, gender, sexual
orientation, religion, handicapped status, or political affiliation. The
organization's link may be removed for this reason whether or not such negative
communication appears on the organization's internet site itself;
      (4)   Poor technical performance. The City may remove a link if attempts
to access the site by the City or any other user reveal poor technical
performance (e.g., slow loading or exiting time, incomplete or unclear display
of text or graphics, difficulty navigating the site, etc.);
      (5)   Obsolete information. The City may remove a link if, in the sole
judgment of the City, the majority of the information displayed on an internet
site is no longer current or relevant, either to the site's stated purpose or
the City's goals, as stated in Section
 177.02(b).
   (d)   Disclaimer. The City is not responsible for the content of any
internet site to which it grants a link or for the availability of such a site
or its content. The City makes no warranty or representation, express or
implied, with respect to the quality, content, accuracy, completeness,
currency, freedom from computer virus or non-infringement of proprietary
rights, of any of the design, information, text, graphics, images, pages,
interfaces, links, software or other materials and items contained in or
displayed on such sites. All such items and materials are provided on an "as
is" basis, and anyone accessing them is fully and solely responsible for their
use of them and any consequences and results of the City, and are subject to
change without notice from the City. In no event shall the City or its
agencies, officers, employees, agents, or representatives be liable for any
direct, indirect, special, punitive, incidental, exemplary, or consequential
damages arising from anyone accessing or using sites linked to the City's
internet site.
(Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.06 ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS FOR BANNERS.
   In addition to the regulations set forth in Section
177.04, the following regulations shall apply to the erection and removal of
banners:
   (a)   Every application to erect a banner shall include a provision, signed
by the applicant, providing that the applicant will indemnify and hold harmless
the City in the event any injury or damage is caused by the placement of the
banner over the public right-of-way, and shall further be accompanied by each
of the following documents:
      (1)   A certificate of liability insurance from a reputable insurance
carrier naming the applicant as insured, and the City as an additional insured,
providing policy limits of not less than $2,000,000.00 for personal injury and
property damage. Each such certificate of insurance shall state that its
coverage is primary for each covered event relating to the erection of the
applicant's banner over Lorain Road; and
      (2)   Written consent from any utility company to erect the banner upon
its poles.
   (b)   Banners shall only be permitted to be erected in the airspace above
the street area of Lorain Road, midway between East Park and West Park Drives,
upon utility poles on either side of Lorain Road at that location.
   (c)   Banners shall be made of vinyl material, and each letter or number on
the banner shall consist of a separate piece of vinyl securely adhered to the
banner; each letter or number on a banner shall be at least twelve inches (12")
in height.
   (d)   All banners shall have "air holes" of sufficient size and number to
prevent the banner from being torn, damaged or destroyed by wind, rain or other
elements of the weather.
   (e)   No banner shall be more than three feet in height, nor more than
ninety feet in length.
   (f)   Banners shall be delivered by the applicant to the City Service
Department for erection no later than five (5) working days prior to the
approved date for erection; banners shall be erected, and removed, solely by
City employees.
   (g)   No banner shall be permitted to be erected more than two weeks prior
to the date of the single event announced, or more than two weeks prior to the
date of the first event of a recurring event announced; the City shall remove
the banner and return it to the applicant within three (3) days following the
date of the occurrence of the single event announced or within three (3) days
following the date of the first event of a recurring event.
      (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.07 PRIORITY IN CASES OF CONFLICT; TIME LIMITS.
   (a)    The following provisions for priority in cases of conflict pertain
solely to the airspace as described in Section
 177.01(a)(1) and the changeable copy signs as described in Section
177.01(a)(2) and (3):
      (1)   Applications for single event announcements shall not be accepted
if the event announced occurs more than one (1) year after the time of
submission of the application.
      (2)   In cases where multiple applications have been received for
simultaneous posting of proposed announcements, the following order of priority
shall apply: the first application filed with the City shall have priority over
all subsequently filed applications. Announcements from the City shall always
have priority over announcements requested pursuant to this section.
   (b)   The following provisions for time limits pertain to all City media as
described in Section
177.01(a), except for the airspace as described in Section
177.01(a)(1):
      (1)   Announcements for community events in the City shall not be erected
or displayed in the relevant nonpublic forum(s) more than two weeks prior to
the date of the single event announced, or more than two weeks prior to the
date of the first event of a recurring event announced.
      (2)   The applicant shall remove all announcements, flyers, and ground
signs within three (3) days following the date of the occurrence of the single
event announced or within (3) days following the date of the first event of a
recurring event. If the applicant does not remove the announcements within
three (3) days, the materials are deemed abandoned and shall be disposed of by
the City. Failure to remove announcements, flyers and ground signs as required
herein may constitute grounds for denial of future requests.
         (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.08 APPEALS FROM DECISIONS OF MAYOR’S DESIGNEE.
   (a)   Every decision of the Mayor's designee denying an application to
announce a community event, or denying an organization's request to link to the
City's website, may be appealed to a Community Access Board consisting of the
Mayor or his designee, the Director of Public Safety, and the Director of Human
Resources. Any such appeal must be in writing and filed with the Mayor's
designee within seven (7) workdays following the date of the mailing of the
decision denying the application.
   (b)   The Community Access Board shall hear the appeal of the applicant,
shall permit the applicant to offer evidence in support of its application, and
shall render its decision no later than ten (10) work days following the date
upon which the appeal was filed. No decision shall be made by the Community
Access Board until it has first consulted with the City Director of Law. In
reviewing appeals made, the Community Access Board shall uphold the decision of
the Mayor's designee only if the Board concludes that either the application or
the proposed announcement violates at least one provision of this chapter.
Every decision of the Community Access Board shall be considered a final
administrative order, subject to further appeal pursuant to the provisions of
Chapter 2506 of the Ohio Revised Code.
(Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.09 NON-ENDORSEMENT POLICY OF CITY.
   A decision to allow a community organization to announce an event, or to
allow a link to the City's website, should not be construed as an implied
endorsement by the City of the aims, goals, or activities of the organization
represented; nor should such decision be construed as implying a preference for
that organization over other organizations of the same type. Furthermore, the
absence of an announcement or link by an organization of a type otherwise
represented should not be construed, by itself, as evidence of a denial of
access to that organization. (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.10  CONTENT REGULATIONS FOR DESIGNATED DISPLAY CASES AND LAWN AREAS.
   The City is establishing a nonpublic forum in the City for display cases as
described in Section
177.01(a)(4) and limited lawn areas on public property as described in Section
177.01(a)(5). Only the announcement of community events by community
organizations or the announcement of an event for which an individual has
rented Springvale Ballroom or the Community Cabin are permitted in such limited
purpose nonpublic forums. Accordingly, any proposed message must be a single
event announcement. No content of any announcement will be edited by City
personnel. Exclusionary criteria for evaluating community announcements are
limited to the following restrictions:
   (a)   Announcements in the City display cases as described in
 177.01(a)(4) must be in the form of one single page flyer or brochure not
exceeding 8.5 in. by 11 in. in size. Following approval from the Mayor's
designee, the applicant is responsible for making any and all copies of the
flyer or brochure for display in the City display cases.
   (b)   Announcements on public property as described in
177.01(a)(5) must be in the form of not more than two (2) ground signs as
described in Section 1163.02(c) and must be made from durable and weatherproof
materials. The ground signs shall not exceed eight (8) square feet in area per
face, and four (4) feet in height above grade. Signs shall not be placed in a
manner that interferes with traffic sight lines.
      (Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)
177.11  ADOPTION OF POLICY AND PROCEDURE FOR CITY MEDIA AND CITY WEBSITE;
PUBLICATION OF REGULATIONS.
   The City shall, by and through the Mayor or his designee, publicize the
regulations established in this Chapter for use of city media and website. The
City may adopt such policy and procedure manual as may be reasonable and
necessary to efficiently implement the provisions of this Chapter, including
but not limited to identification and designation of specific display cases and
lawn areas located within or upon public property. Such policy and procedure
shall be consistent with the standards established herein and must be approved
by the Mayor, following legal review by the Director of Law, before
implementation.
(Ord. 2010-105. Passed 9-21-10.)

179.01 ESTABLISHMENT.
   Pursuant to the authority of the Charter,
Article V Section 1, there is hereby established the Department of Economic and
Community Development. The staffing of the Department of Economic and Community
Development is hereby established and is reflected in the organizational chart
for the Department of Economic and Community Development contained in Section
179.99(a), which is incorporated herein as if fully rewritten. The Mayor shall
establish the compensation of all employees of the Department within the salary
ranges established by City Council, to the extent that such compensation is not
otherwise established by contract, or federal, state or local law.
(Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)
179.02 DIRECTOR OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT.
   The Department of Economic and Community Development shall be headed by the
Director of Economic and Community Development who shall be responsible for the
administration and implementation of plans and programs for the comprehensive
and orderly development of the City. The Director shall be responsible for the
development, maintenance, periodic update and administration of the City's
Master Plan and Planning and Zoning Code. The Director shall provide guidance
to the Mayor, Council, boards and commissions regarding public and private
development within the City.
   (a)    Appointment, Term, Removal. The Director shall be a full time
employee appointed by the Mayor, which appointment and term shall be governed
by Charter
Art. III, §5(a). The Mayor may remove the Director with the concurrence of two-
thirds (2/3) of the members of Council eligible to vote.
   (b)    Duties. The Director of the Department of Economic and Community
Development shall be the head of the Division of Engineering and shall have
charge of all staff within the Department. The Director shall develop policies
to facilitate the orderly and comprehensive development and redevelopment of
the City. She or he shall also initiate programs, plans and strategies for the
retention, expansion and location of businesses, offices and industries in the
City. The Director of Economic and Community Development shall administer and
implement economic development programs and projects to preserve and enhance
the economic sustainability of the City. The Director shall also perform such
other duties consistent with the position as may be required by the Mayor and
such other duties as reflected in the job description on file within the Office
of Director of Human Resources.
Additionally, any references in North Olmsted Codified Ordinances to the
“Planning Director,” “Planning and Development Director” and “Director of
Planning and Community Development” shall mean the Director of Economic and
Community Development, who shall perform such duties assigned therein.
      (Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)
179.03  ADMINISTRATIVE SECRETARY.
   There is hereby created the position of Administrative Secretary, which
shall be a full time employee appointed by and answerable to the Director of
Economic and Community Development. The Administrative Secretary shall perform
the duties as required and directed by the Director of Economic and Community
Development.
(Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)
179.04  PLANNER.
   There is hereby created the position of Planner, which shall be appointed by
and be answerable to the Director of Economic and Community Development. The
duties of the Planner shall include but not be limited to assisting the
Director in the administration and implementation of plans and programs for the
orderly development of the City, reviewing public and private development
plans, and advising boards and commissions on planning matters as necessary.
The Planner shall perform such other duties consistent with the position as may
be required by the Director and such other duties as reflected in the job
description on file within the Office of Director of Human Resources.
(Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)
179.05 ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COORDINATOR.
   (a)   There is hereby created the position of Economic Development
Coordinator, which shall be appointed by and be answerable to the Director of
Economic and Community Development. The duties of the Economic Development
Coordinator shall include but not be limited to
      (1)   Synthesizing raw research into narrative writing for grant
applications, economic development marketing, planning documents, and
government report;
      (2)   Creating economic development marketing collateral in print and
digital formats; and
      (3)   Assisting in the creation and execution of economic development
business attraction, retention, and expansion activities.
   (b)   The Economic Development Coordinator shall perform such other duties
consistent with the position as may be required by the Director and such other
duties as reflected in the job description on file within the Office of
Director of Human Resources.
(Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)
179.06  DIVISION OF ENGINEERING.
   There is hereby created a Division of Engineering within the Department of
Economic and Community Development. The Division of Engineering shall be headed
by a City Engineer, who is a civil engineer registered as a professional
engineer in the State of Ohio. The City Engineer shall be appointed by and be
answerable to the Director of Economic and Community Development.
   (a)    Duties. The City Engineer's duties and responsibilities shall be to:
      (1)    Supervise all personnel of the Division of Engineering.
      (2)    Advise the Mayor, the Council, and administrative departments in
connection with all civil engineering matters of the City related to
engineering, zoning, building, sewers, development and repair of property in
the City, including but not limited to the streets therein.
      (3)    Examine and approve all sidewalks, grading, draining, curbing,
paving, placing of lines, sanitary sewer, storm sewer and water curb
connections and all other utilities of any nature within the right of way of
City streets, alleys, roads and boulevards.
      (4)    Examine and approve or disapprove all grading, draining or
construction within the City, examine and approve or disapprove all plans for
subdivisions and the installation or improvement of private streets, sanitary
sewers, storm sewers and appurtenances, and to examine and approve or
disapprove all lot splits and consolidations.
      (5)    Exercise continuing control and inspection of public installations
and public improvements while work is in progress.
      (6)    Prepare and update all City zoning and street maps.
   (b)    Employees. The staffing of the Division of Engineering is hereby
established and is reflected in the organizational chart for the Department of
Economic and Community Development contained in Section
 179.99(b), which, as it pertains to this Division only, is incorporated herein
as if fully rewritten.
      (Ord. 2023-19. Passed 3-7-23.)

TITLE NINE - Judicial
Chap.
191. Municipal Court.
CHAPTER 191
Municipal Court
   EDITOR'S NOTE: The provisions of Ohio R.C. 1901.01 established the Rocky
River Municipal Court which, pursuant to Ohio R.C. 1901.02, has territorial
jurisdiction within the corporate limits of the City of North Olmsted among
other municipalities. The powers, duties and proceedings of the Court are
established by Ohio R.C. Chapter 1901. Ohio R.C. 1901.25 provides that the
Municipal Court may provide by rule how jurors shall be chosen. Jurors' fees in
any criminal case involving the violation of a North Olmsted ordinance shall be
paid out of the City Treasury. The Municipal Court, pursuant to Ohio R.C.
1901.26(A), may establish a schedule of fees and costs to be taxed in any
action or proceeding, whether civil or criminal. Ohio R.C. 1901.31(F) provides
that fines received for violation of North Olmsted ordinances shall be paid
into the City Treasury. Rule 13 of the Ohio Traffic Rules as promulgated by the
Ohio Supreme Court provides that a court may establish a Traffic Violations
Bureau and specifies certain restrictions as to the designated offenses and
schedule of fines to be accepted as waiver payment in lieu of court appearance.
